name: Spades
tagline: Partners bid their tricks. Spades are always trump. Watch your bags.
rulesSummary: Partners sit across from each other. Everyone bids how many tricks they'll take; 0 is nil.
Follow suit if you can. Spades are trump and can't be led until one has been played (unless you hold nothing else).
Make your team's bid: 10 × bid, plus 1 per extra trick (a bag). Miss it: −10 × bid.
Nil scores ±100; a nil player's tricks don't count towards the partner's bid but do count as bags. Every 10 bags costs 100.
Blind nil: a side 100 or more behind may bid nil before looking at their cards, for ±200. Partners then swap two cards.
First team to the target wins; if both sides are level, play another hand.

Three players: everyone for themselves, 17 cards each (the last card is out of play). The 2♣ leads (the 3♣ if the 2♣ is out). Make your bid for 10 a trick; each trick over it costs 10, and missing costs 10 × the bid. Anyone falling to −200 loses, and the leader wins.
Six players: three pairs, partners across; two packs without the 2♦s (102 cards), 17 each. If two identical cards fall on the same trick, the second one wins.
